name: John Stankey

career.title: Entry-level hire rising through operating roles to Executive Vice President, Industry Markets
Chief Information Officer, then Senior EVP and Chief Technology Officer
Chief Strategy Officer and Group President; later CEO of AT&T Entertainment Group after the DirecTV acquisition

background_rationale: Spent his entire career inside Pacific Bell, SBC and AT&T, running regional operations, technology and business units before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: In a memo to employees, Stankey said AT&T was moving toward a "more market-based culture" with five-day in-office work at hub locations, and that those needing remote or hybrid schedules would have difficulty aligning with the company.
AT&T completed its $5.75 billion all-cash acquisition of Lumen's consumer fiber business, adding more than 1 million fiber customers and over 4 million fiber locations in 11 states.
AT&T committed to invest more than $250 billion through 2030 to build fiber and wireless networks across the United States.
AT&T completed its $23 billion purchase of low- and mid-band wireless spectrum licenses from EchoStar, a deal announced in August 2025.

personal_story.hook: John Stankey joined Pacific Bell straight out of college in 1985; 35 years later he became CEO of AT&T.
personal_story.summary: Stankey grew up in Los Angeles, the youngest of three children of an insurance underwriter and a stay-at-home mother. An Eagle Scout, he worked after school at a sporting goods store stringing tennis rackets, which he has said taught him how businesses decide what they can and can't do. After earning a finance degree from Loyola Marymount in 1985 he joined Pacific Bell, and while working in the Los Angeles cellular business during the late-1980s boom he earned a UCLA MBA, where strategy professor Richard Rumelt pushed him toward 'second-order thinking.' He moved up through the Baby Bell consolidations into SBC and AT&T, running technology, strategy, entertainment and WarnerMedia before taking over as CEO in July 2020.
